leaks: Beef jerky 30 g x 2 snacks/day ('Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate') - commercial beef jerky is soy-sauce marinated and standard soy sauce is wheat-brewed, so this single line item hits TWO of my four walls (soy and gluten). The food row carries allergenTags: null, mayContain: null and no gluten-free/soy-free qualifier anywhere.
Mustard 20 g in 'Chuletas de Cerdo a la Criolla' - unqualified prepared mustard routinely carries wheat flour as a bulking agent. I am coeliac; I cannot take that on trust.
The swap I was offered made it worse: 2 of 3 alternates RAISED jerky from 30 g to 45 g - 'Avocado Chips & Jerky' and 'Pistachios & Jerky'.

delights: The solver refuses to lie about a bad fit: 'Tried 4 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance - closest was "Avocado Chips & Jerky" (landed 250 kcal vs a 191 target).' It told me it had failed instead of quietly serving me a wrong-sized snack. That is the most trustworthy thing in the product.

The grocery list is honest about its own limits: '5 of 31 item(s) have no price match and are excluded from the total (rough CAD estimates for the rest, not sourced data)' - 31 items, sectioned into produce/protein/pantry/spices, CAD 16.53.

'Bahia-style Moqueca prawn stew' is a genuinely appealing real dish with real method steps, and it is naturally clean against all four of my walls - prawns, lime, coconut milk, tomato, rice. If the whole day looked like this I would have paid.

defects.what: I asked to GAIN weight and it prescribed a large deficit - the rate is subtracted regardless of which way my goal points. This is the headline failure: on this plan I lose roughly 1.25 lb/week while trying to gain 1.5 lb/week.
defects.snippet: profile: startWeightKg 89 -> goalWeightKg 93.9, rateLbPerWeek 1.5, targetKcal 2317. By the app's own numbers: Mifflin BMR 1785 x its own formwork-concrete multiplier 1.55 = 2767 before any training, plus weights MET 3.5 x 89 kg x 1 h x 4/wk = ~178/day, so maintenance is ~2945-3067. 2317 = TDEE - 750, and 1.5 lb x 500 = 750.

defects.what: A dish named 'Classic Eggs' contains no eggs. I am not vegan, my dietaryStyle is 'none', and eggs are not on my exclusion list - nothing in my profile asked for an egg replacer, and 300 g of flax-egg slurry is not a portion any human eats.
defects.snippet: MEAL#2 'Classic Eggs & Bell Peppers with Rice' -> ingredients: flax eggs 300g, White rice cooked 145g, Bell peppers 75g, Olive Oil 10g

defects.what: That meal's protein is fictional, and the app knows it. The 'flax eggs' row is carrying egg white's numbers verbatim, which the app admits in its own data - so the 36.8 g protein credited to the meal is off by about 25 g (real flax egg is ~1.3 g protein per 45 g, so 300 g gives ~8 g).
defects.snippet: flax eggs, kcal 55 P 10.7 - dataQuality: 'exception:provenance-cleared - carried fdcId 747997 ("Eggs, Grade A, Large, egg white"), whose description does not denote this food; this row's macros are that record's values verbatim and are therefore NOT this food's numbers'

defects.what: My four medical walls appear to be enforced by name-matching only. Every single food row I inspected - including the jerky - has an empty allergen field, so a composite product cannot possibly be caught. That is why 'Beef jerky' walked straight through a soy AND gluten exclusion.
defects.snippet: Beef jerky | cat=protein | kcal=410 P=33 F=26 C=11 | allergenTags=None mayContain=None | dq: None

defects.what: The same snack twice in one day, at $6.75 a serving each - $13.50/day for 60 g of jerky and 30 g of pork rinds. That is not a snack plan, it is the same bag opened twice.
defects.snippet: SNACK#0 Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate $6.75 / SNACK#1 Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate $6.75 - identical ingredients (Beef jerky 30g, Pork rinds 15g) and identical macros (205 kcal, P19.1)

defects.what: The swap flow rejects the very alternate it just offered me. Applying an alternate by its recipeId 400s; it only works if the client replays the entire ingredients array back. As a customer this is 'the swap button just errors'.
defects.snippet: PUT /api/plans/{planId}/slots/{slotId}/apply with {"recipeId":"cmrevpcyh004gwl5gnni3al5q"} -> 400 {"error":"a slot needs at least one ingredient"} (the alternate had just been returned WITH two ingredients: Bacon 30g, Eggs 75g)

defects.what: Customer-facing copy tells me to go edit a source file. I am a formwork carpenter holding a shopping list, not a developer.
defects.snippet: cost note on every grocery item: 'rough manually-entered CAD estimate, not sourced pricing data - edit src/lib/groceryPrices.js to correct'

defects.what: Two meals are not meals. 310 g of egg white (about ten egg whites) with 220 g quinoa and a whole 120 g onion, no seasoning and 5 g of oil, is an ingredient list. I would not eat it and I would never put it in front of my 13-year-old.
defects.snippet: MEAL#3 'High-Protein Egg White & Onions with Quinoa' -> Egg White 310g, Quinoa 220g, Onion 120g, Olive Oil 5g

defects.what: The two cost figures the app shows me disagree by roughly 2x, with no explanation of which to trust when I am budgeting.
defects.snippet: sum of per-recipe costPerServing across the day = $33.76, but the generated grocery list totalEstimatedCostCad = 16.53

followUp.action: Asked for alternates on the second of my two identical jerky snack plates - it was both my repetition complaint and the item I cannot eat as a coeliac - then tried to swap one in.
followUp.howItWent: Alternates returned 3 options with admirably honest 'none fit within tolerance' warnings, but 2 of the 3 answered my jerky problem with MORE jerky (30 g -> 45 g); only 'Bacon & Eggs' escaped it. Applying that alternate by its recipeId alone was rejected 400 'a slot needs at least one ingredient', and only went through once I replayed the full ingredients array myself - after which the day sat at 2389 kcal, still hundreds below what a lean bulk needs, and snack #0 still holds the jerky I cannot eat.

verdict: The solver is precise, the diagnostics are refreshingly honest, and the moqueca is a dish I would genuinely cook - but it fed a declared coeliac 60 g/day of unqualified soy-sauce-marinated beef jerky, named a dish 'Classic Eggs' that contains no eggs and whose protein it knows is the wrong food's numbers, and prescribed a 600-to-750-calorie daily deficit to a man who told it he wants to gain 11 pounds.
